conviction_note: Balanced: peer prints (TCS cc +0.5% QoQ with $9.6bn TCV, HCLTech raising its FY27 floor, Accenture +22% on an above-street FY27 guide) and Q1 deal decisions that 'slipped to quarter 2' point to a Q2 at or above the -0.5% to -1.4% cc bar, but the ADR has already run +7.2% in five sessions on that read-through, Wipro guided below the street's hoped range on three of its last four prints, and two client losses (Meta cut ~25%, Estee Lauder to Accenture) weigh on the Q3 guide that the stock trades on; a 14-day-to-cover ADR short adds squeeze risk on relief. impact_sum +0.3 from small offsetting findings; p_up 50 x abs_move 4.0 gives 0, and the two measurements agree that there is no edge here.
bar: Q2 FY27 IT services revenue guide $2.574-2.627bn, -1.5% to +0.5% QoQ cc (company, https://upstox.com/news/market-news/earnings/wipro-q1-results-net-profit-rises-0-6-yo-y-to-3-360-crore-q2-revenue-guidance-at-1-5-to-0-5-cc/article-197059/). Street (Kotak Neo preview, 2026-10-14, https://www.kotakneo.com/news/stocks/wipro-q2-fy27-results-preview/ and TradingView/Moody's poll https://www.tradingview.com/news/moodys:ab25a0f6a0c64:0-wipro-q2-preview-brokerages-expect-weak-revenue-growth-margin-recovery/): IT services cc -0.5% (MOFSL, JM) to -1.4% (Jefferies), Emkay and Nuvama -1% USD; IT services EBIT +20 to +50bp QoQ to ~16.2-16.5% (from 16.0%); consolidated revenue Rs 24,885-24,924 cr, PAT Rs 3,335-3,410 cr; Q3 FY27 guide expected -2% to 0% QoQ cc (Emkay, Nuvama). Two or more agreeing sources, so not capped.
positioning_check: WIT ADR short interest 102.75M shares at 2026-09-30 settlement, 14.18 days to cover, up from 62.96M (2026-08-14) and 84.54M (2026-08-31); 1.0% of total shares outstanding, but the ADS count is not sourced so % of ADS float is unknown and some of it may be ADR/local arbitrage (https://equibles.com/stocks/wit/shortinterest, read 2026-10-14). No usable option chain: no skew; front-expiry put/call OI 3.42 on only 615 contracts total (baseline). Run-up +7.19% 5d, +6.55% 20d, 41.5% below the 52-week high; the ADR trades at parity with Mumbai (Rs 170.35 on 2026-10-14 / ~95.5 INR = ~$1.78 vs $1.79).

findings.finding: Peers that reported after Wipro last spoke printed stabilising demand: TCS Q2 FY27 cc revenue +0.5% QoQ, TCV $9.6bn, stock +5.5% (2026-10-09); HCLTech raised its FY27 cc guide floor to 2.5-4% from 1-4% with bookings +27% YoY to $3.26bn (2026-10-12); Accenture beat with a FY27 3-6% LC guide and record bookings and rose ~22% (2026-10-01). Against Wipro's -0.5% to -1.4% cc consensus this argues for a print at or above the middle of the -1.5%/+0.5% guide; but Infosys cut its FY27 guide to 1.5-3.0% in July and Cognizant guides Q3 +3.8-5.3% cc, i.e. peers gaining share in Wipro's weak Americas/healthcare book.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Rebuilt from Yahoo daily closes on confirmed release days (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/WIT?range=1y&interval=1d): 2025-10-16 -2.6%, 2026-01-16 -7.4% (day mapping flagged uncertain), 2026-04-16 +1.4%, 2026-07-16 +0.5%. In Q1 Wipro's cc decline (-1.2%) was better than Citi/Nuvama's -1.4/-1.5% yet the INR revenue missed and the stock was flat: quarter beats have not been paid.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the ADR went from $1.67 (10-08) to $1.79 (10-14), +7.2% in five sessions, and Mumbai from ~Rs 164 to Rs 170, which is what a priced sector read-through looks like. What remains is that the brokerage numbers in the 10-14 preview were set with the guide in mind and have not moved toward the peers' stabilisation.
findings.independence: HCLTech: https://www.freepressjournal.in/business/hcltech-net-profit-rises-21-to-5132-crore-in-q2-fy27-revenue-up-115 ; Accenture: https://www.ibtimes.com.au/accenture-shares-surge-after-earnings-outlook-1876149 ; counterweight Infosys July cut: https://upstox.com/news/market-news/earnings/infosys-q1-results-fy-27-revenue-growth-guidance-narrowed-to-1-5-3-0-in-constant-currency/article-197461/ . All are peer proxies, not Wipro's own number.

findings.finding: On the Q1 FY27 call (2026-07-16) management said some deal decisions 'have actually slipped to quarter 2', that EMR softness in Europe/APMEA should ease as recently won deals come into delivery, and that BFSI client insourcing 'is behind us'; the street (PL Research) models Q2 deal wins of only $2.7-2.8bn against Q1 total bookings of $3.37bn ($1.63bn large deals, 13 large deals), so slipped Q1 decisions closing in Q2 give upside to the bookings line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26 (Oct 2025): bookings 'soared' but weak guidance hit the stock, ADR -2.6% (https://ticker.finology.in/discover/market-update/wipro-q2-fy26-results-analysis-deal-wins). Bookings strength has been overridden by the guide before.
findings.why_not_priced: The bookings estimate in the preview ($2.7-2.8bn) sits below Q1's actual; if the slipped decisions were priced, previews would carry a bookings number at or above Q1. No Q2 large-deal press releases were found (only an ABB renewal on 2026-09-01), so the street has nothing to update on.
findings.independence: PL Research bookings estimate via https://www.tradingview.com/news/moodys:ab25a0f6a0c64:0-wipro-q2-preview-brokerages-expect-weak-revenue-growth-margin-recovery/ ; ABB renewal https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/Cslogin_01092026153716_PressRelease01092026.pdf . Management's own statement, one document.

findings.finding: Two client losses weigh on the Q3 FY27 guide: Mint (2026-08-02/03) reported Meta cut its ~$100M/yr Wipro outsourcing account by at least 25% to ~$75M, replacing the work in-house, and Business Standard (March 2026) reported Estee Lauder moving a ~$500M multi-year contract (~$100M/yr per one source) to Accenture. Combined run-rate loss is up to ~$30M a quarter, ~1.1% of the $2.6bn quarterly IT services base, landing as transitions roll off, likely in H2 alongside Q3 furloughs; the rest of the book (Europe/UK/Nordics healthy, ramping deals) has to offset it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: April 2026: client-specific issues (a delayed large ramp and a slowing banking client) produced a -2% to 0% guide; Mumbai -4%, ADR -2.3% the next day (https://www.outlookbusiness.com/markets/wipro-shares-slip-4-after-q4-brokerages-flag-concerns-despite-buyback).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the street's Q3 guide expectation is -2% to 0%, which presumably carries furloughs and some of this. Neither loss has been confirmed by Wipro, so its size and timing in the guide is unknown to the market; if it were fully in the price the expected guide band would sit below -2% at the bottom.
findings.independence: Estee Lauder: https://scanx.trade/stock-market-news/orders-deals/wipro-faces-potential-100-million-revenue-loss-as-accenture-wins-est-e-lauder-contract/34143171 (single-outlet, unconfirmed); healthcare 'sustained pressure' on the Q1 call https://www.webull.com/news/15239831956513792 .

findings.finding: Wipro has guided below what the street wanted on three of its last four prints: January 2026 Q4 guide 0-2% vs a 1-3% analyst expectation (Morgan Stanley cut to underweight), April 2026 Q1 guide -2% to 0% read as weak visibility, July 2026 Q2 guide -1.5% to +0.5% 'subdued' even including a full quarter of the Mindsprint acquisition; management said in July it would not forecast beyond Q2 and gave no timeline for its 17-17.5% margin target. The street now expects a Q3 guide of -2% to 0%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ADR on guide days: 2025-10-16 -2.6%, 2026-01-16 -7.4% (mapping uncertain), 2026-04-16 +1.4% then -2.3% next day, 2026-07-16 +0.5% (Yahoo daily bars). The guide is the line this stock trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: The 7.2% five-day run-up into the print, on peer relief, raises the bar for the guide; if a weak guide were priced the ADR would not have rallied into the event. Offset: the -2% to 0% expectation already sits at the low end, so the pattern is a lean, not a number.
findings.independence: April: https://www.bajajbroking.in/share-market-news/wipro-q4fy26-results-revenue-steady-sequential-growth-guidance-of-2-to-0-percent-rs150-billion-buyback-approved ; July: https://upstox.com/news/market-news/earnings/wipro-q1-results-net-profit-rises-0-6-yo-y-to-3-360-crore-q2-revenue-guidance-at-1-5-to-0-5-cc/article-197059/ . Shares the reaction data with finding 3; different documents.

findings.finding: FX into Q2 was close to the guide's assumptions: the rupee closed 95.45 (2026-09-10) and 95.74 (2026-09-24) against the guide's USD/INR 94.50, a ~1% weaker rupee that supports INR revenue and margin (street already expects +20-50bp IT services margin); GBP/USD slid from 1.358 (08-28) to 1.334 (09-18) against the 1.34 assumption and EUR/USD ~1.16 matched, so USD-reported revenue should sit near cc.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1: rupee depreciation partly offset wage and AI-investment costs, margin still fell 130bp to a 15-quarter low (https://www.indiainfoline.com/news/companies/wipro-q1-fy27-results-profit-rises-marginally-margins-fall-to-15-quarter-low-stock-gains-1-77).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: brokerages cite currency tailwinds in their margin expansion. Macro-to-company proxy, not confirmed by Wipro.

findings.finding: The WIT ADR short has grown from 62.96M shares (2026-08-14) to 102.75M (2026-09-30), 14.18 days to cover against ADR volume, into a stock 41.5% off its high; the ADR rose 5.9% on 2026-10-13 alone and +7.2% over five sessions, so a relief print or a less-bad guide has a covering mechanism behind it, and a negative is damped.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: the ADR fell 16.9% on 2026-07-01 on a JPMorgan downgrade while Mumbai rose 2%, a liquidity-driven ADR/local disconnect (https://letsdatascience.com/news/wipro-shares-slip-after-adrs-drop-steeply-4df20522): the ADR can move away from Mumbai on flows alone.
findings.why_not_priced: Days to cover rising from 7.5 to 14.2 in two months says shorts were adding, not covering, into the event; the 10-13 jump may be the start of covering. Caveat: the ADS count is not sourced and part of the short may be a hedged ADR/local arbitrage, which would not squeeze.
findings.independence: Price path from Yahoo daily bars https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/WIT?range=1y&interval=1d ; none independent on the short itself.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-08 the US Labor Department suspended Wipro (with TCS, Infosys, HCLTech, Cognizant, Capgemini, Microsoft, Adobe) from the PERM green-card certification programme, halting new and pending applications; the call on 10-15 is the first chance for management to quantify any cost or delivery impact.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Sector shrugged it off: on 2026-10-09 all 10 Nifty IT stocks rose despite the suspension, Wipro +3% intraday (https://www.theweek.in/news/biz-tech/2026/10/09/nifty-it-up-more-than-1000-points-three-reasons-it-stocks-are-rallying-today.amp.html).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced as sector-wide; only a Wipro-specific quantification on the call would move it.
